topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogenesis and cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Mutation, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a somatic evolutionary process driven by a mixture of endogenous cellular errors, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites contribute to malignancy, focusing in detail on the cooperative mechanism of malaria and Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical processes by which physical radiation and chemical agents are converted into reactive compounds that form DNA adducts and induce genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, chemical promoters, and host developmental timing stimulate the proliferation and clonal outgrowth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to evaluate carcinogens, ranging from mutational signatures and population biobanks to in vivo animal tests and the in vitro Ames assay.

topics.label: Concluding Remarks and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic frames everyday exposure in terms of personal risk-benefit analysis and summarizes the core themes of the lecture.
